A1.justification: Both supplied PDFs are readable and describe the same work, with matching methods and main results. v1 includes supplementary Sections A–H; v2 ends after the references. This is an identifiable omission from v2, not an extraction failure.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, user-study scores, ablations, computational measurements, and qualitative application results, including supplementary demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results in Tables 1–6 and the main qualitative and application results in Figures 1–7.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same foundation-feature integration, all-to-all-pair correlation, 3D-GRU refinement, temporal convex upsampling, and training loss. Removing the supplementary implementation explanation and pseudocode does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The training and stereo-evaluation datasets and the 3D tracking application remain unchanged. Demonstrated application coverage narrows: Appendix F and Figure S2's fog and lighting effects disappear, leaving only a general reference to supplementary visual-effects applications in Section 4.5.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding retained experiments, including RAFTStereo, IGEVStereo, Selective-IGEV, DynamicStereo, and BiDAStereo. DepthCrafter and UniDepth also retain their respective comparisons. The added related-work citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported training regimes, metrics, 256×512 crops, 120k/80k training budgets, and training/evaluation sequence lengths and refinement counts remain unchanged. Supplementary split and user-study details disappear, but no replacement settings or revised protocol are reported; this is documentation loss under D1.

E4.justification: All numerical ablations in Tables 4–5 remain unchanged. v2 removes Appendix F/Figure S2's application case study examining the consistency of depth-guided fog and lighting effects. Most other omitted supplementary material consists of qualitative benchmark results rather than distinct ablation or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained tables use the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Every numerical entry in Tables 1–6 and the main figure results remains unchanged. However, Figures S2–S15 disappear, removing visual-effects outcomes, an additional reconstruction, and the supplementary qualitative comparisons. This eliminates the proposed method's ground-truth visual comparisons across all four synthetic evaluation datasets, substantially reducing qualitative result coverage.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 and their mathematical content remain unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs. The omitted upsampling pseudocode and implementation explanation do not constitute a removed formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same architectural novelty, temporal-consistency, zero-shot generalization, and state-of-the-art claims, including the stated improvements of at least 15%.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of foundation priors, correlation, and temporal upsampling, along with Section 4.6's computational-cost and textureless/transparent-region limitations. The omitted application commentary reiterates the existing temporal-consistency interpretation rather than establishing a different explanation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Removing supplementary Sections A–E loses the 10-participant scoring protocol, VDA resizing and normalization instructions, feature-channel details, upsampling pseudocode, exact evaluation subsets and sequence lists, and comparator checkpoint choices. These details are not incorporated into v2's main text. Main training hyperparameters and the project URL remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Accurate and Efficient Stereo Matching via Attention Concatenation Volume and IGEV++: Iterative Multi-range Geometry Encoding Volumes for Stereo Matching, listed as v2 references 65 and 67. Research positioning otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main prose and section order are almost unchanged, apart from trivial wording and citation edits. However, v2 removes the entire structured supplementary narrative, Sections A–H, without relocating its explanations, substantially contracting the document structure while retaining references to that supplement.

P2.justification: v2 removes Figure S1's pseudocode display and the complete supplementary visualization collection, Figures S2–S15. Main Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–6 retain their content, with tighter spacing and layout adjustments. The major difference is the loss of explanatory and comparative displays.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the central method and numerical evidence but removes essential reproducibility information, particularly evaluation sequence selections, preprocessing, checkpoint choices, and the user-study protocol. It also loses substantial qualitative evidence while continuing to direct readers to the absent supplement. The limited citation additions and tighter layout do not offset this substantial loss of reproducibility and evidential completeness.
